scope: Corollary F.9 (Coefficient equidistribution and one-site consequences) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 144. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the hypotheses and symbol estimate of Lemma F.7. The coefficient arrays of Ch(x + V t) are equidistributed to any prescribed accuracy against the bounded-cost Fourier approximations used in the tilt, jointly with the spatial smooth weights and bounded-modulus congruences. Consequently Z = 1 + o(1) in Equation (F.4). Mixed centers give the one-site approximation in item 1 of Proposition F.2; with fixed centers the one-site law has negligible excess mass above a pre-bounded density relative to uniform measure on U. Noninjectivity has negligible probability.
